claims.text: An AlCoCrFeNi-based HEA will exhibit superior elevated-temperature tribo-corrosion resistance compared with conventional structural alloys.
AlCoCrFeNi-based alloys are multi-principal-element high-entropy alloys.
The multi-principal-element makeup promotes in situ formation and retention of a stable protective oxide or passive film.
The protective film is rich in Al2O3 and/or Cr2O3.
The protective film remains stable during simultaneous thermal and mechanical loading.
Conventional structural alloys suffer rapid wear and corrosion under combined high-temperature and tribological conditions.
Compositional tuning of an AlCoCrFeNi-based HEA can enhance passive-oxide formation.
The surface oxide layer will persist and self-heal under simultaneous mechanical and chemical stress.
The HEA's multi-element design promotes solid-solution strengthening.
Oxidation of Al and Cr causes rapid passivation and produces a compact, adherent oxide film.
The oxide film acts as a barrier that slows further oxidation.
The oxide film reduces mechanical material loss during tribological contact.
Under identical conditions, the tailored HEA will have significantly less combined wear and corrosion loss than conventional alloys.
Reduced combined material loss will provide improved long-term durability in extreme environments.
Traditional Inconel-type alloys and duplex stainless steels lack the compositional flexibility needed to form an enduring passivating layer under harsh tribo-corrosion conditions.
The protective effect applies only while temperature and wear remain below the limits at which the oxide film degrades.
Extreme fluctuations or overly aggressive tribological loads may compromise passive-film formation.
The magnitude of improvement depends on alloy composition, processing route, temperature, mechanical load, and corrosive medium.
